mcqs.q: Among hunting dogs that retrieved wild fowl in Washington State, what proportion had antibodies to H5/N1 subtype influenza A?
mcqs.e: Antibodies were detected in 4/194 (2%) of the hunting dogs sampled.

mcqs.q: What distinguished the seropositive dogs in this study?
o: They had high levels of exposure to waterfowl
They had been vaccinated against influenza
They had no contact with birds
mcqs.e: Owner-reported history showed seropositive dogs had high levels of exposure to waterfowl.

mcqs.q: Which clinical sign was the most distinguishing feature of leptospirosis in this Venezuelan outbreak cohort?
mcqs.e: Conjunctival suffusion was reported as the most distinguishing clinical sign, with many patients also showing liver involvement.

mcqs.q: What reservoir was implicated in spreading Leptospira to both cows and humans in this outbreak?
mcqs.e: The same Leptospira species found in humans were isolated from local rodents, and phylogenetics suggested a rodent-spread expanding outbreak strain.

mcqs.q: The PB2 substitutions E627K and D701N found in the cat-derived H5N1 viruses are associated with what?
o: Adaptation of the virus to mammals
mcqs.e: E627K and D701N in the polymerase basic protein 2 gene are markers of mammalian adaptation.

mcqs.q: How did the cat-derived H5N1 isolates behave in ferrets?
o: They caused fatal infection and spread by contact between ferrets
They infected only the inoculated animal
They required injection to cause disease
mcqs.e: Both isolates caused fatal infections and demonstrated contact transmission between ferrets, indicating high pathogenicity and mammalian transmissibility.

mcqs.q: Which animal exposure was most strongly associated with cutaneous sporotrichosis in this Thai cohort?
mcqs.e: 65.3% of patients reported cat exposure, and cat contact was significantly associated with upper-extremity lesions (adjusted OR 18.9).

mcqs.q: Which oral monotherapy was effective for cutaneous sporotrichosis, with a median time-to-cure of about 180 days?
mcqs.e: Oral itraconazole monotherapy was effective (all isolates had itraconazole MIC <1 µg/mL); median time-to-cure was 180 days.

mcqs.q: What did the survey identify as a key barrier for non-specialist UK practices dealing with highly pathogenic avian influenza?
o: A lack of confidence in treating birds and handling suspected cases
mcqs.e: A lack of confidence around treating birds and dealing with suspected HPAI cases was a key barrier that limited client education opportunities.

mcqs.q: What was a stated limitation of this survey?
o: A small, self-selected group of respondents who may over-represent avian-interested vets
mcqs.e: Only 26 self-selected veterinarians responded, possibly over-representing those with existing avian/HPAI interests.

mcqs.q: Why does heat treatment (HT) of samples increase the sensitivity of heartworm antigen tests in dogs?
o: It disrupts antigen-antibody immune complexes that block antigen detection
It detects host antibody instead of antigen
It has no real effect on sensitivity
mcqs.e: In some infected dogs antigen is blocked by immune complexing, causing false negatives; heat treatment disrupts these complexes and unmasks antigen (12 extra positives in this study).

mcqs.q: Which screening combination, recommended by the American Heartworm Society, improved diagnostic performance in this shelter-dog study?
mcqs.e: Pairing point-of-care antigen with microfilaria detection improved sensitivity without loss of specificity, consistent with AHS recommendations.

mcqs.q: Even using combined testing, the study estimated it may have missed approximately how many infected dogs?
mcqs.e: Combined POC antigen and microfilaria screening still may have missed more than one in four infected dogs.

mcqs.q: What is the current Dirofilaria status of the United Kingdom according to this review?
o: Still considered non-endemic but at risk of establishment
mcqs.e: The UK is still considered non-endemic with only limited non-autochthonous cases, but is at risk of outbreaks.

mcqs.q: Which factors could change the UK's non-endemic status for Dirofilaria?
o: Climate change combined with spread of invasive mosquito species
mcqs.e: A combination of climate change and potential spread of invasive mosquito vectors may expose the UK to filarial outbreaks.

mcqs.q: In this southern Italy survey of nearly 2,000 dogs, which filarial species was detected most frequently?
mcqs.e: D. immitis was the most frequent species (11.4% prevalence), followed by D. repens (3.7%) and A. reconditum (0.6%).

mcqs.q: Which dogs were significantly more likely to be infected with D. immitis?
mcqs.e: Sheltered dogs, mongrels, and animals housed in rural areas were significantly more infected.

mcqs.q: What was the prevalence of heartworm preventive use in the Golden Retriever Lifetime Study sample?
mcqs.e: Heartworm preventive use prevalence was 39.5% in this cohort.

mcqs.q: Which factor was associated with GREATER odds of heartworm preventive use?
o: Being in the top quartile of height
Receiving vaccinations and living in the Southern United States
mcqs.e: Receiving vaccinations and Southern US location (among others) were associated with greater odds; supplement use and tallest height quartile were associated with lower odds.

authors: Rajković M, Glavinić U, Bogunović D, et al.

mcqs.q: What effect did natural Dirofilaria immitis infection have on canine leukocytes in this comet-assay study?
o: It caused DNA damage, greatest in dogs with severe clinical signs
It had no measurable genotoxic effect
mcqs.e: D. immitis infection induced leukocyte DNA damage, with the highest damage in dogs showing severe clinical signs.

mcqs.q: Which 'slow kill' regimen reduced DNA damage and eliminated microfilariae over the treatment period?
mcqs.e: Treatment with ivermectin and doxycycline decreased leukocyte DNA damage and progressively eliminated microfilariae.

mcqs.q: What treatment protocol did antigen/microfilaria-positive dogs receive in the Linosa Island elimination program?
o: Oral doxycycline for 4 weeks plus monthly topical imidacloprid/moxidectin
mcqs.e: Positive dogs received oral doxycycline twice daily for 4 weeks plus monthly topical imidacloprid/moxidectin for 12 months.

mcqs.q: By month 2 of the elimination program, what was the microfilariae status of the island's dogs?
mcqs.e: After a 76.5% reduction in month 1, from month 2 onward all animals were microfilariae-negative.

mcqs.q: The Linosa Island heartworm program was described as an example of what concept?
mcqs.e: Treating positive dogs plus chemoprophylaxis reduced human infection risk, representing a One Health paradigm.

mcqs.q: Compared with dogs that had successful adulticidal heartworm treatment versus dogs that never tested positive, what long-term risk was found?
o: Significantly elevated risk of right heart failure, left heart failure, and cardiomyopathy
Lower risk of all cardiac disease
Only an increased risk of skin disease
mcqs.e: Treated dogs had significantly elevated long-term risks of right heart failure (RR 3.59), left heart failure (RR 1.83), and cardiomyopathy (RR 2.79).

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about heartworm preventive purchase compliance and the risk of a positive heartworm test?
o: Compliance had no effect on risk
Even lapsed preventive purchase was associated with lower risk of a positive test than no purchase at all
Injectable preventives performed worse than monthly ones
mcqs.e: Dogs with lapses in preventive purchase still had reduced risk versus no purchase (monthly RR 0.36; injectable RR 0.15), underscoring the value of compliance.
